title: PISA: Piecewise Sparse Attention Is Wiser for Efficient Diffusion Transformers
claim: Our approximation-based sparse attention matches dense-attention quality and attention patterns at much lower cost, while prior block-sparse methods degrade.
layout: 4 panels: two stacked video-frame rows, image grid, attention heatmaps; metrics in colored captions
description: The top half shows two rows of six video frames of a calico cat with a carrot and tissues. Row (a) is dense attention with a red latency label of 1468 s. Row (b) is PISA (Ours) with a green label of 687 s, a 2.14x speedup and PSNR 24.69. The frames look nearly identical. The bottom left, panel (c), is a grid of FLUX.1 images (taxi, umbrella, man, cat in a hat). Each has three columns: Dense, Ours at r=85%, and SpargeAttn at r=80%. PSNR and LPIPS values are overlaid, and SpargeAttn is visibly worse. The bottom right, panel (d), has three green heatmaps of attention maps: Dense, PISA, and Sparse. Dense and PISA look alike (L1 error 1.36%, FLOPs 20.4%). The sparse map is mostly blank, with 10.34% error. Red and green text marks bad and good numbers.
caption: \textbf{\ourmethod{} accelerates diverse generation tasks.} (a, b) Wan2.1-14B image-to-video generation. (c) FLUX.1 image generation. \ourmethod{} achieves better quality than SpargeAttn at higher sparsity. (d) Wan2.1-1.3B attention patterns: \ourmethod{} more closely approximates dense attention than block sparse attention at similar cost.
abstract: Diffusion Transformers are fundamental for visual generation, but their efficiency is bottlenecked by the quadratic complexity of self-attention. While block-sparse attention accelerates computation by attending only to critical key-value blocks, it suffers from quality degradation at high sparsity due to discarding substantial context. In this work, we discover that attention scores of non-critical blocks exhibit distributional stability, allowing their contributions to be accurately and efficiently recovered rather than dropped. Motivated by this insight, we propose PISA, a training-free Piecewise Sparse Attention that covers the full attention span via lightweight compensation for skipped non-critical blocks. Unlike the conventional "keep-or-drop" paradigm that directly drops non-critical blocks, PISA establishes the "exact-or-approximate" paradigm: it preserves exact computation for critical blocks while approximating the remainder through block-wise Taylor expansion around block centroids. This design allows PISA to serve as a faithful proxy to full attention, achieving 1.91$\times$ and 2.57$\times$ speedups on Wan2.1 and Hunyuan-Video, and 1.2-1.6$\times$ acceleration on FLUX without compromising quality. Code is available at: https://github.com/xie-lab-ml/piecewise-sparse-attention.
